dial.summary: September NFP shocked at +29K (vs 90K consensus, August revised down to +133K), sharply reducing October FOMC hike odds and catalyzing a DXY reversal from pre-NFP highs of 102.20 to an Oct 2 close of 101.88 — still a headwind above 100 but the directional shift is constructive; BTC held above $85,900 with BTC.D firm at 58.5% and perpetual funding rates ticking only to ~0.0100% (well below the 0.04% overheating threshold), confirming unlevered spot accumulation continues; 2s10s curve steepened to +49bps on the dovish labor print while real yields held at 2.88% — BTC Accumulation posture intact, with October 14 CPI and October 27–28 FOMC as the next major catalysts for a macro regime shift.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) remains at ~$103.7T based on August 2026 data — September G4 M2 not yet available (6–8 week reporting lag); US M2 confirmed at $23.3T for August 2026 per Fed H.6 (highest ever), contributing to the G4 aggregate; China M2 at ~$53.2T, Eurozone ~$18.7T; 4-week trend flat: no new confirmed September G4 data to establish direction; YoY still meaningfully positive (not contracting); status neutral — confirmed rising 4-week trend required for supportive; weak September NFP (+29K) and ISM manufacturing prices at 77.9% present a stagflation signal that complicates the liquidity expansion narrative; next G4 M2 update expected mid-November 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: September 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI = 54.5%, released October 1 — ninth consecutive month of manufacturing expansion; 4-week trend flat: August 54.6% → September 54.5% = −0.1pp, within the flat threshold (<0.5% relative change); New Orders Index rose 1.6pp to 55.3% (bullish forward signal); Production Index 56.7% (−1.6pp); Prices Index at 77.9% (highest since mid-2021, a leading inflation signal complicating Fed's response to September's soft NFP at +29K); status neutral (above 50 but flat; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 or above 62); October ISM Manufacturing releases November 3.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY closed at ~101.88 on October 2, 2026 — rallied to intraday highs above 102.20 (fresh 2026 highs) before the September NFP release, then fell to the 101.80 area post-data as payrolls missed badly (+29K vs 90K) and October FOMC hike odds collapsed; prior October 1 close was ~102.09; 4-week trend up: ~99.8 (Sep 3) → 101.88 (Oct 2) = +2.1% over 30 days, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind — DXY still above 100 threshold despite post-NFP pullback; a sustained close below 100 required to return to neutral; October 14 CPI is the next major DXY repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) at 2.88% as of October 1, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.15 (Sep 30 reading was 2.93%); 10Y nominal yield ticked to ~5.27% on October 2 despite the weak NFP (+29K), reflecting stagflation concerns from ISM Prices Index at 77.9%; 4-week trend up: ~2.50% (Sep 3) → 2.88% (Oct 1) = +38bps over 30 days; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% absolute threshold both met); breakeven inflation ~2.28–2.39% (stagflation premium building); a sustained fall below 2% required to shift status to neutral; October 14 CPI is the next key real yield repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: October 2, 2026 post-NFP: 10Y Treasury at 5.27% (ticked higher despite weak jobs — stagflation/fiscal concern), 2Y at 4.78% (fell as October FOMC hike odds collapsed after +29K NFP miss) → 2s10s spread = +0.49% (+49bps); prior October 1: +0.44% (+44bps); 4-week trend up (steepening): Sep 3 spread ~+42bps (10Y 4.762%, 2Y 4.342%) → Oct 2 +49bps = +7bps steepening over 30 days, above the 5bps flat threshold; status supportive (both positive AND steepening on 4-week basis); post-NFP curve steepening driven by 2Y falling faster than 10Y as Fed hold expectations rose sharply; October 14 CPI and October 27–28 FOMC are the next major yield curve catalysts.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,743,031M ($6.74T) for week ending September 30, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.4.1 released October 1; weekly progression: Sep 2: $6,737,204M → Sep 9: $6,740,619M → Sep 16: $6,746,548M → Sep 23: $6,747,704M → Sep 30: $6,743,031M (slight week-over-week decrease of $4.7B); 4-week trend flat: Sep 2 $6,737,204M → Sep 30 $6,743,031M = +$5.8B over ~4 weeks, marginal expansion within flat threshold on a $6.74T balance sheet; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no QT acceleration announced at Sep 15–16 FOMC where FFR raised to 3.75%–4.00%); weak September NFP (+29K) raises probability of a Fed hold in October, supportive for balance sheet stability.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate ticked up to approximately 0.0100% per 8h as of October 2–3, 2026 (up from 0.0067% on September 30 per CoinGlass); open interest rose ~$2.3B since September 30 as BTC crossed $86,500 per CoinDesk — funding rates rising alongside OI signals growing directional bias but rate remains well below the 0.04% overheating threshold; BTC price ~$85,900–86,500 as of October 2; BTC.D firm at 58.5% (alts underperforming); 30-day funding rate consistently sub-0.010% historically, current tick-up reflects spot rally rather than leveraged speculation; status supportive (significantly below 0.04% overheating threshold); October 14 CPI and October 27–28 FOMC are next potential funding regime catalysts.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$308B as of early October 2026 (up from ~$292B on October 2); total crypto market cap ~$2.89T (BTC.D 58.5%); stablecoin dominance ~10.45%; 30-day trend flat: ~10.4% (Sep 3) → ~10.45% (Oct 3) = +0.05pp over 30 days, within the flat threshold; status neutral — dominance is not falling on a 30-day basis (not supportive) and total crypto market cap is roughly flat-to-down (not the rising-while-dominance-rises headwind condition); stablecoin supply expansion to $308B reflects continued institutional adoption and DeFi demand rather than pure risk-off flight; BTC.D rising from ~56.5% (Oct 1) to 58.5% (Oct 2–3) as alts underperformed the BTC spot rally; status downgraded from supportive as 30-day falling trend reversed to flat.

upcoming.title: ISM Services PMI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Services PMI for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — services sector is ~80% of US GDP; context: September NFP already shocked at +29K (vs 90K consensus), so a strong ISM Services print above 55 would confirm a late-cycle bifurcation between softening labor and resilient services — the most challenging stagflation scenario for the Fed; S&P Global Flash Services PMI surged to 58.7 in September (59-month high), a strong leading indicator; prior August ISM Services was 54.2%; a print above 56 would sharply complicate the dovish narrative triggered by the NFP miss and may revive October FOMC hike speculation; the combination of ISM Manufacturing at 54.5%, ISM Prices at 77.9%, and a +29K NFP frames this as a high-stakes release for the October 27–28 FOMC setup.

upcoming.title: FOMC Minutes (September 15–16, 2026 Meeting)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases minutes of the September 15–16 FOMC meeting at 2:00 PM ET — the meeting at which the Fed raised the fed funds rate 25bps to 3.75%–4.00%; minutes will reveal debate around further tightening pace, any dissents, and how the committee framed the balance between inflation (ISM Prices 77.9%, CPI ~3.5% YoY) and employment risks; critical to parse for October hike signals given that September NFP came in at +29K post-release, which the committee could not have anticipated; market is now pricing a high probability of a Fed hold at October 27–28 FOMC; minutes will show whether the committee was already leaning toward a pause or if the NFP miss is a surprise to their baseline.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended October 4, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ended October 4, 2026 — the first weekly claims reading fully incorporating October's early labor conditions in the wake of the shocking September NFP (+29K); prior weeks approximately 206K; closely watched for signs of labor market deterioration confirming the NFP miss is a trend rather than a one-off; consecutive claims above 225K would reinforce the dovish pivot narrative and cement Fed hold expectations for October 27–28; released the day after FOMC Minutes, providing a real-time confirmation or rebuttal of the September labor story.
